description: The outline a crawler, a screen reader, and an agent all read the same way. Structure is the only part of a page that survives being stripped of its styling, which is exactly the form every machine reader sees it in.

gates.title: One h1 Per Route
gates.rule: Exactly one h1. Several h1 elements leave nothing stating what the page is about, and the outline has no root to hang the rest of the headings from.
gates.fix: Keep the one that names the page and demote the rest to h2.

gates.title: Routes That Render Headings Open With h1
gates.rule: A route with headings starts at h1. Starting at h2 because it looked smaller is styling decided in the markup, and it costs the page its top-level subject.
gates.fix: Promote the opening heading to h1 and set its size in the stylesheet.

gates.title: No Heading Level Is Skipped
gates.rule: Levels descend one at a time. An h2 followed by an h4 tells a machine reader a section is missing, and the outline it builds is wrong in a way nothing on the rendered page reveals.
gates.fix: Renumber the headings so each step down is one level.

gates.title: The Page Has Landmarks
gates.rule: main, nav, header and footer exist as elements or roles. The accessibility tree is the cleanest signal an agent reads, and a page built entirely from div elements gives it nothing to orient on.
gates.fix: Replace the wrapper divs with the semantic elements they already stand in for.

gates.title: Anchor Text Says Where It Goes
gates.rule: No link whose entire label is a placeholder. The anchor text is what the destination ranks for, so a site full of `read more` links passes its ranking signal to nothing.
gates.fix: Replace each placeholder with the destination's subject.

gates.title: Every Route Links Onward
gates.rule: Each route carries at least one outgoing link. A route linked from nowhere and linking to nothing is reachable only through the sitemap, and passes nothing on to the rest of the site.
gates.fix: Add links from each route to the related routes a reader would want next.

gates.title: A Breadcrumb Trail Exists
gates.rule: The site renders a breadcrumb trail. It is the one navigation element Google shows in place of the raw URL in a result, and it tells a reader where the page sits before they open it.
gates.fix: Render a breadcrumb nav on nested routes and mark it up as BreadcrumbList.

gates.title: Interaction Lives On Real Controls
gates.rule: Clicks are bound to buttons and links, not to divs and spans. An agent reading the accessibility tree finds nothing it can act on, and a keyboard reaches none of it.
gates.fix: Swap each clickable div for a button or an anchor and let it keep its own styling.
